> I don't know if the problem is with VS Code on Windows or with the extension itself.

If Godot crashes, the issue is probably with Godot. So please provide the requested information.

An LSP trace is available through the "Output" panel in VSCode. Just select the "Godot LSP" output stream and set the log level (cog icon) to "Trace". (Set the log level before reproducing the issue, it only takes effect for new messages.)

As for a crash log. Please provide the output of Godot. This can be done e.g. by launching Godot from Power Shell.

VS Code Godot LSP:
```

```
After 17 seconds, Godot shuts down and the extension attempts to reconnect to it.

```
Editing project: C:/Users/nicol/Documents/Godot/Godot Projects/FNF Godot
```

No errors appear in either case, both in PowerShell and VS Code
Your log level is set to "info" not "trace".

1. I suspect this is related to the no root environment (rootUri == null, rootPath == null -> this means you are viewing a single file without viewing the whole project). However I have no clue how to reproduce this, because for me the VSCode extension does simply not try to connect to Godot in this mode.

Regardless:

2. Does the error occur for you when opening the whole project (opening the folder in VSCode instead of the file).
3. Does the error occur in 4.6 beta 1. Does the error occur in 4.5.stable?

4. Your Godot output does not seem complete. Might be some windows thing related to how the project manager starts projects. Please start the project directly using `--editor --path ...`.

> 2. Does the error occur for you when opening the whole project (opening the folder in VSCode instead of the file). Yep, also happens. > 3. Does the error occur in 4.6 beta 1. Does the error occur in 4.5.stable? In Godot 4.6 beta 1, the extension fails to connect for some reason, stating it's a "Wrong Project": `Godot 4.5.1 Stable` - Only version `2.4.0` of `godot-tools` connects to godot; versions 2.5+ don't detected the application. > 4. Your Godot output does not seem complete. Might be some windows thing related to how the project manager starts projects. Please start the project directly using `--editor --path ...`. I ran the command `--editor --path "C:\Path"` with the VS Code closed, and the standard messages appeared. After loading the game files, I opened the editor, and incredibly, nothing about error or anything appeared. Regarding the other questions, I will test them now.

In summary, the extension in `Godot 4.5.1 stable` works normally in version `2.4.0`, But starting with version 4.5 it crashes every time I try to open any file in Godot format (`.gd, .tscn, etc`), regardless of the version. 

In version `2.5.+` of the extension, for some reason it doesn't connect correctly to Godot.

I used previous versions of the extension, and it only crashes on `4.6`. It works normally in versions `4.5.1` and below.

> 1. However I have no clue how to reproduce this, because for me the VSCode extension does simply not try to connect to Godot in this mode. I'm not sure how is this different for you because for me on Windows 10 it's trying to connect to Godot even when I open one GDScript file from my project in VS Code. And I don't even have Godot open. Is it an OS-dependent behavior? That doesn't sound good.

I tried it in the following:

Rider,
Windsurf,
Codium

All would show a massive amount of errors in the code, despite showing that language server was connected successfully, then Godot would crash. 

It happened only on beta2. beta1 and 4.5 current worked fine.
I am viewing the project root, not opening a single file as a project.

System:
Godot v4.6.beta2 - KDE neon User Edition 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (RADV NAVI32) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900K (32 threads) - 125.6 GiB memory

@HolonProduction I have narrowed this down to a circular reference with two scripts preload()ing each other. In my case that was caused by the ProtonScatter add-on.

The crash occurs when both scripts are assigned to a `const` rather than a `var`:

test.gd:
```
extends Node

const t2 = preload("res://test2.gd")
```

test2.gd:
```
extends Node

const t = preload("res://test.gd")
```
